text.p: A surge in the price of lead and the benefits of several years of cost-cutting are expected to propel lead and zinc producer Pasminco Ltd to a 150 percent jump in profits for the year to June 30, analysts said.
Analysts' average forecast for Pasminco's 1995/96 net profit before abnormal items was A$42 million compared with A$16.7 million a year ago.
Forecasts ranged from A$35 million to A$57 million.
"Most of the major influence would be the very extensive cost cutting they've done over the last several years and also higher lead prices," one Sydney-based analyst told Reuters.

Lead prices averaged US$0.33 a pound a during fiscal 1995/96, up from 28 cents over the previous year, an analyst noted. He said Pasminco's profit would rise by A$4 million to A$5 million for every one cent rise in the price of lead.
Another analyst said Pasminco also stood to benefit from a two to three cent premium for lead sold into the burgeoning Asian markets.
"Their natural market is going through a unprecedented boom time and there aren't many (lead) warehouses there," he added.
